completeCurrentGoal.title: Herstellung und Struktur von Silikonen für Polymervergleiche erklären
completeCurrentGoal.titleEn: Explain silicone formation and structure for polymer comparison
completeCurrentGoal.description: Die lernende Person kann Herstellung und Bau von Silikonmolekülen beschreiben und daraus ihre Eigenschaften im Vergleich mit ausgewählten kohlenstoffbasierten Polymeren erklären.
completeCurrentGoal.descriptionEn: The learner can describe production and structure of silicone molecules and use that account to explain their properties in comparison with selected carbon-based polymers.

extendedData.sourceDutySplitAuthorStatus: HOLD independent source, graph, A/M, P, D and V review; native course labels are technical metadata, not a new source approval

scope: Targeted followup resolving the earlier independent B child1 property-comparison finding; complete goal and whole profile/cases inspected within this boundary.

fullCreditComparisonFinding.before: The old e2 rubric allowed full credit for backbone comparison and separation of chains/network points. Old e3 could be satisfied by the oil counterexample and missing heat/long-term data without comparing observed PE permanent deformation with network-PDMS recovery.
fullCreditComparisonFinding.after: Complete corrected case2 task 2, DE/EN model answers, e2 criteria/full-credit/partial-credit rules and profile e2 observable performances explicitly require the supplied PDMS recovery versus PE permanent deformation comparison under equal testing conditions.
fullCreditComparisonFinding.specificRequiredObservedComparison: Crosslinked PDMS recovers after extension; the supplied PE specimen retains deformation under the same test conditions.
fullCreditComparisonFinding.universalPEBackboneCauseForbidden: C–C identity alone is neither the cause of every PE deformation nor proof of a universal property ranking; the corrected answer and zero-credit rule explicitly reject that inference.
fullCreditComparisonFinding.independentScientificReasoning: The supplied PE result is an observation for a particular specimen. Covalent network constraints explain recovery of the specified PDMS material; PE deformation is not assigned to backbone identity alone.

retainedChemicalDuties.formation: Silanol condensation creates new Si–O–Si links with water elimination.
retainedChemicalDuties.endGroupsAndValences: Two terminal OH groups remain; each Si has four single bonds, internal bridge oxygen two and terminal OH oxygen one Si and one H bond.
retainedChemicalDuties.networkBoundary: The linear bifunctional-silanol tetramer condensation does not itself generate a branched covalent network. The material data separately supply additional covalent links between chains.
retainedChemicalDuties.networkStructureReasoning: Additional interchain covalent links constrain relative sliding and account for recovery in the supplied elastomer; greater chain length alone is not crosslinking.
retainedChemicalDuties.preservedExact: Original case2 data, e1 formation/balance rubric, e3 network/bounded-choice rubric and coverage contract remain exactly unchanged.
retainedChemicalDuties.manufacturingScope: Bounded paper-model production/structure competence; no actual laboratory synthesis, product certification or learner result.

meaningfulTransfer.actualChangedCondition: Same PDMS chemistry, initially unlinked sliding oil chains, then supplied additional interchain covalent links and recovering elastomer.
meaningfulTransfer.requiredInference: Explain how the changed network topology changes the material response, contrast the concrete recovering PDMS and permanently deformed PE, and limit the choice to these specimens/loading rather than generalizing to every silicone/PE or untested temperature/duration.
meaningfulTransfer.shallowResponseThatFails: Naming Si–O versus C–C or merely copying the two observations cannot satisfy the required network explanation and bounded conclusion. Asserting that a longer bifunctional chain automatically becomes a network is also rejected.
meaningfulTransfer.chainLengthChangeAlone: Trimer to tetramer is a balance variation and is not, by itself, accepted as meaningful transfer.

supportingCase1.reason: Correct finite trimer, molecular/backbone distinction, oil/network reasoning and changed-state seal selection are elicited. Only the PE backbone is supplied, with no PE property observations; it cannot alone establish the complete PDMS-versus-carbon-polymer property comparison.

completeCase2.reason: The balanced finite production model, correct molecules/backbones, actual required cross-polymer property comparison, network explanation and conditional judgment are all demanded and graded.

twoIndependentEvidencePiecesPermittedWit.performance: Independently construct and balance the end-group-correct finite tetramer and distinguish backbone links from additional interchain network links.

twoIndependentEvidencePiecesPermittedWit.piece: Changed-condition material inference and bounded comparison
twoIndependentEvidencePiecesPermittedWit.performance: Independently explain the oil-to-network response, compare actual PDMS recovery with actual PE permanent deformation, and justify the case-limited conclusion without a universal backbone cause.

wholeProfileCoverage.futureAssessmentBoundary: Actual learner work must show all required facets and distinct evidence pieces. If supporting case1 is used, the missing property-comparison facet still needs the complete supplied-data comparison in case2 or equivalent evidence. Six points, one task completion or a learner agreement is not automatically mastery.
